observations.statement: Proof size, proof search, and proof verification are distinct resources; an upper or lower bound for one does not automatically transfer to the others.
observations.support: H013-H015 and H014 separate polynomial proof existence, automatability, and polynomial identity testing obligations.

observations.statement: Knowledge-compilation lower bounds for direct representations do not automatically survive the addition of auxiliary variables followed by existential projection.
observations.support: R021 gives explicit exponential succinctness effects from auxiliary variables, so attacks on H016-H019 must match their extension language.

observations.statement: A local compiler is non-circular only when rule radius, semantic certificate size, scheduler, number of steps, output size, interface width, and witness recovery are all explicitly bounded.
observations.support: Without these bounds, global SAT solving can be hidden in rule choice, canonicalization, or an unbounded interface.

observations.statement: Mutually incompatible OPEN hypotheses can coexist in the registry because OPEN records failure of the listed attacks, not simultaneous truth or subjective probability.
observations.support: H012 conflicts with H013, and H007 conflicts with H014, yet no recorded decisive attack settles either pair.

observations.statement: Hash-consing compresses repeated syntax but cannot by itself compress exponentially many semantically distinct residual functions.
observations.support: This is the central attack against H018-H019 and motivates communication-complexity and residual-diversity lower bounds.

observations.statement: For d-DNNF and related tractable languages, satisfiability after compilation is easy; the universal exact compilation bound is the entire unresolved burden.
observations.support: H016 is useful only if a fixed local grammar is proved to terminate with polynomial output on every CNF.
